claims.statement: Local testing guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and requires repository read access, not native publishing/admin authority. It presupposes installed Jekyll and an existing Jekyll site.
Bundler/Ruby setup and macOS installation troubleshooting are recommendations; fetching dependencies executes external code and is not authorized merely by documentation. No source setup executed.

Procedure runs bundle install in publishing source and bundle exec jekyll serve, illustrated with _site output and loopback server on port 4000. Sample console output is not an actual build, test or live-process receipt.
Ruby >=3.0 may lack webrick; source suggests bundle add webrick, which changes dependency manifests/resolution. This is a conditional diagnosis, not an automatically safe dependency edit.
Ruby >=3.2 compatibility errors prompt source suggestion of Ruby <=3.1.x. Historical fallback is not a current supported/security recommendation; no runtime downgrade performed.

serve --baseurl="" deliberately overrides configured baseurl for local preview. Successful root preview would not verify project-subpath URLs, deployed custom-domain routes or hosted configuration parity.
Browser localhost:4000 preview requires observing actual rendered behavior; build success alone does not prove links, access boundaries, content correctness or hosted publication.

Source recommends updating github-pages to reduce local/hosted rendering differences using bundle update github-pages or gem update. Latest available is not proven equal to a particular GHES/cloud server version or an immutable reproducible dependency set.

Actions-preferred deployment note does not invalidate local Jekyll testing or prove custom workflow uses the same runtime. All claims reference-only; no dependencies changed, server started, policy accepted, rights cleared or native rollout verified.
